title: Collection overwrites configured custom-marker classifications
reasoning: The runner honors problem.markers mappings, but collection queries and classifies only built-in markers. Reconciliation then unconditionally replaces the runner's classification. A current-checkpoint test carrying only a custom marker mapped to Error or Functionality becomes Core, changing group counts, collection hashes, and group-based policy outcomes.
reproduction: Configure a custom marker mapped to Functionality and apply it to a current-checkpoint test. Execute through run_checkpoint_with_collection without a -k filter; reconciliation changes its group to Core.
recommendation: Use one classification rule for collection and execution, including custom-marker mappings and the existing precedence rules.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included runner fixture defines no custom markers, and the collection tests do not exercise classification or reconciliation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Exercise custom markers mapped to each group through collection and reconciliation, including combinations with built-in markers and prior-checkpoint tests.
minimumFixScope: Collection marker discovery/classification, shared classification logic, and associated tests.

history.reasoning: All original evidence files still exist, but the implementation changed: collection now discovers custom markers and shares classify_test_group with execution. The repair is incomplete. MarkerConfig uses use_enum_values=True (config.py:88), so classify_test_group returns a string for custom markers (line 112). Collection passes that string to _group_key (collection.py:458), which accesses .value (line 282). Targeted validation with a custom Functionality marker failed with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'value'. Thus the original Core overwrite has been replaced by a collection failure; the custom-marker contract remains broken. No linked patch attempts were supplied.
